guardian_calls.question: I need to add a final "Thank you for your attention" slide to an existing PowerPoint file (Q4_financial_report.pptx). Please provide the full documentation overview and any relevant workflows for editing/adding slides to an existing pptx file.
guardian_calls.response:
# PPTX Skill Documentation Overview This skill covers **creating, editing, and analyzing PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations**. The most relevant parts for adding a final “Thank you for your attention” slide to `Q4_financial_report.pptx` are the **editing existing OOXML** workflow and the **template/workflow scripts** for slide duplication/replacement. --- ## 1. Reading / analyzing a presentation ### Text-only extraction ```bash python -m markitdown path-to-file.pptx ``` Use when you only need the readable text content. It converts slides to Markdown. ### Raw XML access Raw XML is required for: - Comments - Speaker notes - Slide layouts / slide masters - Design elements - Animations - Complex formatting - **Slide structure manipulation** #### Unpack a `.pptx` A `.pptx` is a ZIP archive of XML parts. Unpack with: ```bash python ooxml/scripts/unpack.py ``` If that script path is missing, locate it with: ```bash find . -name "unpack.py" ``` For example: ```bash python ooxml/scripts/unpack.py Q4_financial_report.pptx working/ ``` #### Key file structure | Path | Purpose | |---|---| | `ppt/presentation.xml` | Main presentation metadata, slide references | | `ppt/slides/slide{N}.xml` | Individual slide contents | | `ppt/notesSlides/notesSlide{N}.xml` | Speaker notes | | `ppt/comments/modernComment_*.xml` | Comments | | `ppt/slideLayouts/` | Layout templates | | `ppt/slideMasters/` | Master slide templates | | `ppt/theme/` | Theme/colors/fonts | | `ppt/media/` | Images and media | --- ## 2. Editing an existing PowerPoint (OOXML workflow) **This is the primary workflow for editing or extending an existing file like `Q4_financial_report.pptx`.** ### Required workflow 1. **MANDATORY — read `ooxml.md` in full first.** - Do not set range limits. - This file contains the detailed OOXML structure and exact editing guidance. 2. **Unpack the file** ```bash python ooxml/scripts/unpack.py Q4_financial_report.pptx working/ ``` 3. **Edit the XML parts** - Most slide changes are in `ppt/slides/slide{N}.xml` - If you are adding a slide, you also need to update: - `[Content_Types].xml` - `ppt/_rels/presentation.xml.rels` - `ppt/presentation.xml` - Slide relationships under `ppt/slides/_rels/` 4. **CRITICAL — validate immediately after each edit** ```bash python ooxml/scripts/validate.py working/ --original Q4_financial_report.pptx ``` Fix every validation error before continuing. 5. **Pack the final presentation** ```bash python ooxml/scripts/pack.py working/ updated_Q4_financial_report.pptx ``` ### What usually needs to change when adding a slide When you manually add a slide to an unpacked presentation, you are adding: - A new slide part: `ppt/slides/slide{N}.xml` - A slide relationships part if needed: `ppt/slides/_rels/slide{N}.xml.rels` - A new relationship entry in `ppt/_rels/presentation.xml.rels` - A new `` entry in `ppt/presentation.xml` - A new `` content-type entry in `[Content_Types].xml` If the slide uses **any** media, layout references, images, notes, or comments, the corresponding `.rels` files must also be updated so the new slide part can resolve them. ### Easiest way to add a matching final slide Preserve the existing design by making a copy of a suitable existing slide part, then edit that slide’s copied XML: ```bash cd working/ppt/slides cp slide7.xml slide8.xml cp _rels/slide7.xml.rels _rels/slide8.xml.rels ``` Then: 1. Edit `slide8.xml` to: - Change the title/body to “Thank you for your attention” - Remove old financial report content 2. Update relationships/content-types/presentation references so PowerPoint recognizes slide 8. 3. Validate: ```bash python ooxml/scripts/validate.py working/ --original Q4_financial_report.pptx ``` 4. Pack: ```bash python ooxml/scripts/pack.py working/ updated_Q4_financial_report.pptx ``` > Good candidate slides to duplicate are title slides, section dividers, or any simple “closing” style slide with large centered text. Inspect the thumbnail grid first. --- ## 3. Creating a new PowerPoint from scratch without a template If at some point you need to generate a brand-new deck, use the **html2pptx** workflow. ### Mandatory first step Read `html2pptx.md` **completely** before creating slides that way. No range limits. ### Design requirements - State your content-informed design approach before writing code - Use web-safe fonts only: - Arial, Helvetica, Times New Roman, Georgia, Courier New, Verdana, Tahoma, Trebuchet MS, Impact - Create clear visual hierarchy with size/weight/color - Ensure readable contrast - Be consistent across slides ### Color palette guidance Pick 3–5 colors that match: - The topic - The industry - The tone/mood - Brand identity, if mentioned Some provided palette examples include: - Classic Blue - Teal & Coral - Bold Red - Burgundy Luxury - Cream & Forest Green - Pink & Purple - Black & Gold - Sage & Terracotta - Coastal Rose - Orange & Turquoise - Plus many others in the full documentation ### html2pptx workflow 1. Read `html2pptx.md` fully 2. Create individual HTML files, one per slide, with real dimensions such as `720pt × 405pt` for 16:9 3. Use semantic HTML tags: `

Use the `html2pptx.js` library with the `html2pptx()` function 7. Add charts/tables through PptxGenJS 8. Save with `pptx.writeFile()` 9. Generate thumbnails and validate visually for: - Text cutoff - Text overlap - Bad positioning - Contrast problems --- ## 4. Creating a new presentation from an existing template This workflow is useful when you need to build a new deck while preserving an existing template’s look. ### Steps 1. **Extract and inspect the template** ```bash python -m markitdown template.pptx > template-content.md python scripts/thumbnail.py template.pptx ``` Read the extracted markdown and thumbnail map completely. 2. **Create a template inventory file** Save as `template-inventory.md`: ```markdown # Template Inventory Analysis **Total Slides: [count]** **Slides are 0-indexed** - Slide 0: [layout code] - description - Slide 1: [layout code] - description ... ``` 3. **Create an outline** Map content to the best available slide layouts. Do not force content into a layout that has more placeholders than content; pick the layout that structurally matches each slide. 4. **Duplicate/reorder/delete slides with `rearrange.py`** ```bash python scripts/rearrange.py template.pptx working.pptx 0,34,34,50,52 ``` - Slide indices are 0-based - Repeating an index duplicates that slide - Omitted slides are deleted To append a duplicate of slide 7 to an existing deck with slides 0 through 7, you could use something like: ```bash python scripts/rearrange.py template.pptx working.pptx 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,7 ``` 5. **Extract all text with `inventory.py`** ```bash python scripts/inventory.py working.pptx text-inventory.json ``` Read the entire JSON file. It gives: - Slide/shape structure - Placeholder types - Paragraph text/properties - Bullets, alignment, fonts, colors, spacing 6. **Create `replacement-text.json`** For every text shape you want to replace, add a `paragraphs` field. Example entry: ```json { "slide-0": { "shape-0": { "paragraphs": [ { "text": "Thank You", "alignment": "CENTER", "bold": true }, { "text": "Questions?", "alignment": "CENTER" } ] } } } ``` Formatting rules: - Do not include bullet symbols (`•`, `-`, `*`) when `"bullet": true` - Always include `"level"` when `"bullet": true` - Preserve original alignment, fonts, sizes, and colors where appropriate - Use `color` for RGB, e.g. `"FF0000"` - Use `theme_color` for theme colors, e.g. `"DARK_1"` 7. **Apply replacements with `replace.py`** ```bash python scripts/replace.py working.pptx replacement-text.json output.pptx ``` Important caveats: - The replacement workflow clears **all text shapes from the inventory** unless you provide replacement paragraphs for them - It is designed for full-deck rebuilding, not necessarily for making a single surgical edit inside an existing deck - For preserving all other slides of `Q4_financial_report.pptx`, the raw OOXML editing workflow above is usually safer --- ## 5. Thumbnail grids Create visual grids for analysis and validation: ```bash python scripts/thumbnail.py presentation.pptx ``` Features: - Default 5 columns - Default max 30 slides per grid - Slides are 0-indexed Examples: ```bash python scripts/thumbnail.py Q4_financial_report.pptx workspace/q4-grid --cols 4 ``` Options: - `--cols 3` → 12 slides/grid - `--cols 4` → 20 slides/grid - `--cols 5` → 30 slides/grid - `--cols 6` → 42 slides/grid Use thumbnail grids especially: - When analyzing template layouts - After editing, to visually inspect for layout problems --- ## 6. Converting slides to images Alternative visual inspection path: ```bash soffice --headless --convert-to pdf presentation.pptx pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 presentation.pdf slide ``` Options: - `-r 150` controls DPI - `-f N` starts at page N - `-l N` stops at page N - `slide` is the output prefix Example: ```bash pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 -f 1 -l 5 presentation.pdf slide ``` --- ## 7. Dependencies The skill assumes these tools exist: | Purpose | Install | |---|---| | Text extraction | `pip install "markitdown[pptx]"` | | Creating presentations via html2pptx | `npm install -g pptxgenjs` | | HTML rendering | `npm install -g playwright` | | Icons | `npm install -g react-icons react react-dom` | | SVG rasterization/image processing | `npm install -g sharp` | | PDF conversion | `apt-get install libreoffice` | | PDF-to-image | `apt-get install poppler-utils` | | Secure XML parsing | `pip install defusedxml` | --- ## Direct recommendation for your task For adding a final **“Thank you for your attention”** slide to `Q4_financial_report.pptx` while keeping all existing slides untouched: 1. Use the **raw OOXML editing workflow** 2. First read `ooxml.md` completely 3. Unpack `Q4_financial_report.pptx` 4. Create a thumbnail grid to pick a visually appropriate source slide to duplicate 5. Copy the source slide XML and `.rels` 6. Edit the copied slide XML to make it a clean closing slide 7. Update presentation relationships/content types 8. Validate after each edit 9. Pack the final file If instead you want to use the `rearrange.py`/`replace.py` workflow, remember it is optimized for rebuilding a full deck from a template. Be careful: `replace.py` will clear unlisted inventory shapes, so it can destroy content in slides you did not intend to change.
